name: DropGenius
summary: Generates a Shopify dropshipping store (products, branding and copy) as a starting template, not a finished business. Public buyer reviews cluster on one complaint: charges continuing after cancellation, with no route to a refund.
best_for: absolute beginners who want a pre-built Shopify dropshipping store scaffold in minutes and understand it's a starting point, not a business
skip_if: you want a genuinely free start (the 'FREE store' asked for a card, a $1 trial and a pre-ticked $19 add-on when we tried on 18 November 2026), you are uncomfortable with the documented billing complaints, or you expect an AI-generated store to sell by itself
honest_knock: We have to be blunt here: the dominant theme in DropGenius’s public buyer reviews is unauthorised charges continuing after cancellation with no route to a refund, and some reviewers report never reaching a dashboard to cancel at all, with support emails bouncing back undeliverable. An AI-generated store in 30 seconds is also just a starting template: the product selection, marketing and margins remain entirely your problem. When we tried to sign up on 18 November 2026, the 'FREE store' turned out to need a card for a $1 trial that renews at $99 a month on the preselected plan, with a $19 add-on already ticked. If you proceed: untick what you do not want, pick your plan yourself, pay attention to cancellation mechanics from day one, screenshot everything, and treat the Renewal Radar as mandatory equipment.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Pro · per month billed annually at $288 -- cheaper than the $39 monthly Starter, which is not offered annually at all
pricing.notes: On 18 November 2026 the 'Build my FREE store' button on dropgenius.com sent us to a card form titled 'Pay Securely' on a different domain and brand, app.storebuilder.ai/checkout. It asked for card details for a '7-day trial for just $1. After 7 days, your selected plan renews at $99/month', with Empire ($99) preselected among Starter $39, Pro $59, Empire $99 and Unicorn $299, each $1 for the trial. A 'Get access to Winning Products for $19' add-on and the terms checkbox were already ticked, and a countdown claimed 'Only 26 trial spots left this month due to high demand'. We entered nothing and paid nothing. The monthly prices match the pricing page as re-verified on 19 September 2026 (unchanged since August): Starter $39, Pro $59, Empire $99, Unicorn $299; that page then described a 14-day free trial, which is not what the checkout offered. Switch to annual billing and Starter disappears from the table; the rest become Pro $24/mo (billed annually at $288), Empire $57/mo ($684) and Unicorn $79/mo ($948). The meter is catalogue size: Starter 25 unique products, Pro 250 unique plus 25 premium, Empire 10,000 and 10,000, Unicorn 25,000 and 25,000. The FAQ on their own homepage, re-read the same day, still quotes an older $39.99-$299.99 range plus a $1.99 one-time store-creation fee, so the marketing copy and the pricing table continue to disagree. Nothing anywhere on the pricing page mentions the Shopify subscription the generated store runs on.
